From 6f16886b7c050c934305b1f285c3458ff1b6e4e4 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Sudeep Holla <Sudeep.Holla@arm.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Jan 2016 11:19:29 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] cpuidle: fix fallback mechanism for suspend to idle in
 absence of enter_freeze

Commit 51164251f5c3 "sched / idle: Drop default_idle_call() fallback
from call_cpuidle()" made find_deepest_state() return non-negative
value and check all the states with index > 0.  Also as a result,
find_deepest_state() returns 0 even when enter_freeze callbacks are not
implemented and enter_freeze_proper() is called which ends up crashing
the kernel.

This patch updates the check for index > 0 in cpuidle_enter_freeze and
cpuidle_idle_call(when idle_should_freeze is true) to restore the
suspend-to-idle functionality in absence of enter_freeze callback.

Fixes: 51164251f5c3 "sched / idle: Drop default_idle_call() fallback from call_cpuidle()"
Signed-off-by: Sudeep Holla <sudeep.holla@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Rafael J. Wysocki <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com>

diff --git a/drivers/cpuidle/cpuidle.c b/drivers/cpuidle/cpuidle.c
index 046423b0c5ca..f996efc56605 100644
--- a/drivers/cpuidle/cpuidle.c
+++ b/drivers/cpuidle/cpuidle.c
@@ -153,7 +153,7 @@ int cpuidle_enter_freeze(struct cpuidle_driver *drv, struct cpuidle_device *dev)
 	 * be frozen safely.
 	 */
 	index = find_deepest_state(drv, dev, UINT_MAX, 0, true);
-	if (index >= 0)
+	if (index > 0)
 		enter_freeze_proper(drv, dev, index);
 
 	return index;

diff --git a/kernel/sched/idle.c b/kernel/sched/idle.c
index 34852ee70d54..30f7b6ad3920 100644
--- a/kernel/sched/idle.c
+++ b/kernel/sched/idle.c
@@ -162,7 +162,7 @@ static void cpuidle_idle_call(void)
 	 */
 	if (idle_should_freeze()) {
 		entered_state = cpuidle_enter_freeze(drv, dev);
-		if (entered_state >= 0) {
+		if (entered_state > 0) {
 			local_irq_enable();
 			goto exit_idle;
 		}
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/cpuidle/cpuidle.c`**
   - The condition in the `cpuidle_enter_freeze` function was modified from checking if `index >= 0` to `index > 0`. This change ensures that the `enter_freeze_proper` function is only called when a valid idle state (greater than 0) is found, preventing potential crashes when no `enter_freeze` callbacks are implemented.

2. **File: `kernel/sched/idle.c`**
   - Similarly, in the `cpuidle_idle_call` function, the condition was changed from checking if `entered_state >= 0` to `entered_state > 0`. This adjustment ensures that the code only proceeds to enable local interrupts and exit idle if a valid state (greater than 0) is entered, thus maintaining the suspend-to-idle functionality.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in both files are closely related as they both address the same issue regarding the handling of idle states in the absence of `enter_freeze` callbacks. The change in `cpuidle.c` ensures that the `enter_freeze_proper` function is only invoked for valid states, while the change in `idle.c` ensures that the idle call logic respects this condition. Together, these changes restore the proper fallback mechanism for suspend-to-idle functionality, preventing kernel crashes that could occur when invalid states are processed.
